Subject: Re: legal check — EU VAT implications and risk mitigation

Team — quick legal POV. The cross-entity VAT allocation raises exposure for both parties if the tax treatment is incorrect. Before we finalize the MOU: 

- Require GreenHarbor to provide a completed supplier VAT certificate (we have a template).
- Require statement from their tax team confirming which entity will carry the VAT liability.

If they cannot provide those within 21 days we should:
- Hold 25% of the unpaid balance (to be escrowed on our side) until documentation is provided OR
- Accept the 5% short-pay credit but add explicit acceptance of liability language in the MOU (shifts cost to GreenHarbor if tax authority later assesses VAT).

Laura — need confirmation that escrow/hold accounting is feasible and whether moving 25% to a hold account triggers revenue recognition issues. If hold is not feasible, we should default to the 5% short-pay with legal indemnity language.

-Markus
VP Legal, Redwood Inference
